title: The South Atlantic’s next exploration chapter |
gist: Wood Mackenzie's Lens Subsurface analysis of five South Atlantic offshore basins finds they share the same Early Cretaceous rift geology but sit at very different maturity stages, and argues that on their shared Upper Cretaceous play, the barely-tested Southwest African Coastal Basin is analogous to what a re-imaged ultra-deepwater campaign could unlock in Brazil's mature Santos Basin.

insights.claim: The five most prolific South Atlantic offshore basins — Campos, Santos, Guyana, Côte d'Ivoire and the Southwest African Coastal Basin — share the same underlying geology, having formed when the African and South American tectonic plates rifted apart in the Early Cretaceous.
insights.speaker: Fiona Piggott
insights.so_what: Establishes a single common geological framework across five basins, which is the analytical basis for treating one basin's results as predictive of another's untested potential.
insights.quote: Campos, Santos, Guyana, Côte d'Ivoire and SW African Coastal basins were all formed when the African and South American tectonic plates ripped apart in the Early Cretaceous period.
insights.locator: The South Atlantic oil and gas play's five key basins

insights.claim: Despite sharing the same origin, the five South Atlantic basins sit at very different maturity stages: Santos and Campos are mature, Guyana is mid-cycle with strong momentum, Côte d'Ivoire has yet to deliver a step-change discovery, and the Southwest African Coastal Basin has barely been tested against its mapped prospective area.
insights.speaker: Fiona Piggott
insights.so_what: The maturity spread implies very different risk/reward profiles for capital allocation: Guyana offers proven momentum, while the Southwest African Coastal Basin offers largely untested frontier optionality.
insights.quote: Santos and Campos are mature and Guyana is mid-cycle with strong momentum. Côte d'Ivoire has yet to deliver a step-change, while the Southwest African Coastal Basin has barely been tested against its mapped prospective area.
insights.locator: The South Atlantic oil and gas play's five key basins

insights.claim: Over 1,400 exploration wells have been drilled across the five South Atlantic basins, with roughly a quarter of them resulting in a discovery.
insights.speaker: Fiona Piggott
insights.so_what: A roughly 25% overall discovery rate across 1,400+ wells is a useful base-rate benchmark for evaluating future South Atlantic exploration well economics.
insights.quote: Over 1,400 exploration wells have been drilled across the five basins, with a quarter making a discovery.
insights.locator: The South Atlantic oil and gas play's five key basins

insights.claim: 57% of discoveries across the five South Atlantic basins came from Upper Cretaceous Sandstone plays, making it the dominant reservoir play type in the region.
insights.speaker: Fiona Piggott
insights.so_what: Identifies the specific play type explorers should prioritize when de-risking new South Atlantic acreage.
insights.quote: 57% of those discoveries in Upper Cretaceous Sandstone plays.
insights.locator: The South Atlantic oil and gas play's five key basins

insights.claim: On the Upper Cretaceous play they share, Wood Mackenzie argues the frontier Southwest African Coastal Basin is analogous to what a re-imaged ultra-deepwater exploration campaign in Brazil's mature Santos Basin could deliver.
insights.speaker: Fiona Piggott
insights.so_what: Suggests operators holding legacy Santos Basin acreage may be underestimating remaining running room by treating it as fully mature, when frontier-basin-scale upside may remain in the same play.
insights.quote: Yet on the Upper Cretaceous play they share, the frontier Southwest African Coastal Basin is analogous to what a re-imaged ultra-deepwater campaign in Brazil’s mature Santos Basin could deliver.

insights.claim: Wood Mackenzie's report contends that discovered ultra-deepwater reserves in the Santos Basin understate the basin's true remaining potential.
insights.speaker: Fiona Piggott
insights.so_what: A contrarian read against treating Santos as a fully explored, mature basin — implies unrecognized upside for incumbent Santos operators willing to re-image with modern seismic/subsurface tools.
insights.quote: Why discovered ultra-deepwater reserves in the Santos Basin understate its true potential.

insights.claim: Wood Mackenzie positions one basin approaching 50 years of drilling (Santos, Brazil) and one barely tested basin (Southwest African Coastal) as the two key anchors defining the next chapter of South Atlantic deepwater exploration.
insights.speaker: Fiona Piggott
insights.so_what: Gives investors a simple two-basin framework for tracking South Atlantic exploration newsflow: one for re-imaging upside, one for frontier discovery risk/reward.
insights.quote: The South Atlantic is the defining frontier of conventional deepwater exploration, and two of its anchors look nothing alike: one approaching 50 years of drilling, the other barely tested.

insights.claim: Wood Mackenzie's analysis uses the Conventional Plays dataset within its Lens Subsurface modelling tool to move from high-level benchmarking of the South Atlantic's five key basins to play-level comparison of the Santos and Southwest African Coastal analogues.
insights.speaker: Fiona Piggott
insights.so_what: Identifies the proprietary WoodMac subsurface tooling underlying the analogue claim, relevant for assessing the rigor and repeatability of the basin comparison.
insights.quote: Wood Mackenzie’s expert analysts used the Conventional Plays dataset in our Lens Subsurface modelling tool to move from high-level benchmarking of the region’s five key basins to play-level comparison of the two analogues.

insights.claim: The full underlying Wood Mackenzie report additionally covers where five-basin exploration capex is currently concentrated and where the economics of the Santos and Southwest African Coastal margins diverge, though this article does not disclose those specific findings and gates them behind a downloadable report.
insights.speaker: Fiona Piggott
insights.so_what: Flags that the capex-allocation and margin-economics findings — likely the most directly tradeable data — require obtaining the full gated report rather than being available in this teaser.
insights.quote: Where five-basin exploration capex is currently focused... Where the economics of the two margins diverge, and why.
